company: APA Group (Australian Pipeline Limited as responsible entity for Australian Pipeline Trust and APT Investment Trust)
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: The directors of the responsible entity, Australian Pipeline Limited. Subject to the full section 4.2 regime: Closed Periods, prior clearance from the Chairman (or the ARMC Chairman where the applicant is the Chairman), the short-term and short selling bans, the absolute hedging and derivatives ban, the restrictions on granting security, and the section 4.4 notification obligations.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: The Company Secretary, APA Group's Executive Committee, the Responsible Officers of Australian Pipeline Trust and APT Investment Trust, the directors of subsidiaries in APA Group, and other persons specified from time to time by the Managing Director. The Company Secretary maintains a register and notifies individuals of inclusion or removal. Subject to the same substantive section 4.2 restrictions as Directors; clearance comes from the Company Secretary (or the Managing Director in the Company Secretary's own case) and dealings must be notified to the Company Secretary within two business days.

tiers.name: Related Parties
tiers.description: The spouse (including de facto spouse) or partner of a Director or Designated Person, children of a Director or Designated Person who live with them, and any company, superannuation fund or trust over which a Director or Designated Person has significant influence. Section 4.2 applies to them; Directors and Designated Persons must take all reasonable steps to cause their Related Parties to comply with section 4.2 as if they were Directors or Designated Persons.

tiers.name: employees and contractors
tiers.description: All other employees and contractors of APA Group and its subsidiaries. The policy applies to their dealings, but only through section 4.1 (the insider trading prohibition and the obligation to seek advice from the Company Secretary if in doubt). None of the section 4.2 special rules, Closed Periods, clearance requirements, hedging bans or financing restrictions is expressed to apply to them.

definitions.hedging_definition: any hedging instruments or arrangements regarding or derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person

windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the business day after the release of APA Group's half yearly results to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No express power to impose additional blackouts over APA Securities. The equivalent control is exercised through clearance: outside a Closed Period a Director or Designated Person must obtain clearance, the Recipient consults the Disclosure Committee on whether there is Inside Information that should prevent the dealing, the decision is 'in the absolute discretion of the Recipient and is final and binding', reasons need not be given, a clearance may be withdrawn if circumstances change, and the applicant must keep the application and any refusal confidential. Separately, the Managing Director may from time to time and for any period prohibit or restrict dealing by Designated Persons in Restricted Securities (securities of entities other than APA Group), a blanket prohibition notified by the Company Secretary and extending to Related Parties.

rules.detail: Absolute ban at all times, expressly including outside Closed Periods, on entering derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director. No venue limit, so an OTC put or call written by a bank is squarely caught. There is no clearance route: section 4.2.3 clearance is a gateway to dealing outside a Closed Period, not a waiver of the 4.2.5 prohibition, and the 4.2.7 exceptional circumstances power relieves only against dealing during a Closed Period.
rules.evidence: Directors and Designated Persons are not permitted at any time (including outside any Closed Period) to enter into any hedging instruments or arrangements regarding or derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.

rules.detail: Same absolute ban as for Directors, applying at all times and irrespective of vesting. Extends through section 4.2.6 to Related Parties, whom the Designated Person must take all reasonable steps to cause to comply as if they were a Designated Person.
rules.evidence: Directors and Designated Persons are not permitted at any time (including outside any Closed Period) to enter into any hedging instruments or arrangements regarding or derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over APA Securities held by the Director are equally caught; the prohibition is on the class of instrument, not on where it is traded. A derivative over APA Securities the Director does not hold is not literally within 4.2.5, but would engage the short selling and short-term or speculative trading bans in 4.2.4.
rules.evidence: derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.

rules.detail: Section 4.2, which contains the derivatives ban, applies only to Directors, Designated Persons and their Related Parties. Employees and contractors outside those categories are subject only to the insider trading prohibition in section 4.1, which is silent on derivatives.

The hedging ban is not limited to unvested or plan securities: it reaches any hedging instrument or arrangement regarding any APA Securities held by the Director, so a collar over freely held, vested, unrestricted securities is prohibited. The prohibition is expressed as absolute in time and has no approval or exception mechanism.

Monetisation structures such as prepaid forwards, exchangeable notes and collar-plus-loan packages are not named, but each is a hedging instrument or arrangement regarding APA Securities held by the Director, and the derivative component is a derivative financial product issued over those securities, so all are caught by the at all times ban. An outright disposal remains the only permitted way to realise value, subject to Closed Periods and clearance.

Securities lending and borrowing are nowhere named and are not within the definition of dealing (apply for, acquire or dispose of securities). The nearest analogue is the 4.2.5 condition that a margin loan or secured financing arrangement must not permit title to the APA Securities to be transferred, which is inconsistent with a title-transfer securities lending arrangement, but lending as such is not addressed.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over APA Securities held by the Director is a derivative financial product issued over those securities and a hedging arrangement regarding them, so it is caught by the at all times ban; a short CFD would also breach the short selling ban and, given the 12 month holding expectation, the short-term or speculative trading ban.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly permitted but on two cumulative conditions: the APA Securities must be included in a diversified portfolio, not pledged as a stand-alone or single-stock parcel, and the facility must not permit title to the APA Securities to be transferred. The policy continues to apply to the pledged securities, so they may not be disposed of during a Closed Period without 4.2.7 permission. No disclosure obligation, loan-to-value limit or price trigger guidance is imposed.

Two overlapping tests. First, an intention test: a purchaser should intend at acquisition to hold for at least the next 12 months, with no precise definition of short-term or speculative trading offered. Second, a window test: a Director must not both buy and sell APA Securities in the same open period between two consecutive Closed Periods, save that this does not prohibit the sale of securities acquired under an employee equity incentive scheme or employee security plan.

exemption_authority: Section 4.2.7: the Chairman may approve dealings by Directors, and the Chairman and Managing Director jointly may approve dealings by Designated Persons, during a Closed Period, but only in exceptional circumstances and on a declaration of no price-sensitive information; the ARMC Chairman may act if the Chairman is unavailable. Approval must be in writing in advance and specifies the period during which it is valid, and may be withdrawn if circumstances change. This power relieves only against the Closed Period restriction in 4.2.2 and the clearance requirement in 4.2.3; it is not expressed to waive the section 4.2.5 hedging, derivatives or security-granting prohibitions. Separately, the board of Australian Pipeline Limited may determine that the 4.2.8 exclusions do not apply.
jurisdiction_overlays: Singapore Exchange - APA Group's medium term notes are listed there and the insider trading laws are stated to extend to prohibited activity in respect of APA Securities listed in an overseas jurisdiction, whether undertaken in Australia or offshore

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons are not permitted at any time (including outside any Closed Period) to enter into any hedging instruments or arrangements regarding or derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single clause defeats the funded collar: both the purchased put and the written call are derivative financial products issued over APA Securities held by the executive, and the ban is absolute in time, indifferent to vesting, and has no clearance or exemption route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons may include APA Securities in a diversified portfolio under a margin loan facility or secured financing arrangement provided that: the facility or arrangement does not permit title to the APA Securities to be transferred.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even setting the derivatives ban aside, the loan leg fails on its own terms: a facility secured solely on the collared APA parcel is not a diversified portfolio, and any title-transfer collateral or rehypothecation right is expressly prohibited, so only a non-title-transfer security interest inside a broader portfolio facility is permitted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any APA Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that person, or any third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unvested and holding-locked securities are unavailable as collateral in any structure, and the words 'directly or indirectly' and 'or any third party' block back-to-back or guarantee arrangements over that stock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: to avoid doubt, the terms of this policy will continue to apply to the relevant APA Securities, including the requirement that they not be disposed of in a Closed Period unless permission for such disposal is granted pursuant to section 4.2.7.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A margin call or enforcement sale during a Closed Period is not an excluded dealing and requires exceptional circumstances permission from the Chairman, so a lender cannot rely on unfettered enforcement rights and the borrower bears the timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance to undertake a proposed dealing will be valid for three business days or until a Closed Period commences, whichever is the shorter period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing in the underlying must be priced and executed within three business days, and a clearance may be withdrawn if circumstances change, which constrains any multi-leg execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The decision to give or refuse clearance is in the absolute discretion of the Recipient and is final and binding on the Applicant, and reasons for the decision need not be provided. ... If clearance is refused, the Applicant must keep the fact of that refusal confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no obligation to explain, and the executive cannot tell a bank counterparty why a transaction cannot proceed, so financing documents should not require disclosure of the reason for a refusal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the guiding principle is that Directors and Designated Persons who purchase APA Securities should intend, at the time of acquisition, to continue to hold the purchased APA Securities for at least the next 12 months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any structure with an economic tenor of under 12 months, or that contemplates repurchasing securities delivered under the collar, risks being treated as short-term or speculative trading.

bespoke_clauses.topic: same open period buy and sell
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons must not both buy and sell APA Securities in the same “open” period between two consecutive Closed Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement of a collar combined with any purchase in the same open window would breach this rule, so delivery and any repurchase must straddle a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: APA Group requires that Directors and Designated Persons take all reasonable steps to cause their respective Related Parties to comply with this section 4.2 as if they were Directors or Designated Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared stock through a spouse, resident child, family trust, superannuation fund or significantly influenced company does not escape the hedging ban or the financing conditions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is drafted by reference to securities held, so a cash-settled index or basket derivative not referable to a held parcel is arguably outside 4.2.5, though it would still face the short selling and short-term trading prohibitions in 4.2.4.

bespoke_clauses.clause: other persons specified from time to time by the Managing Director ... The Company Secretary will operate a process for regularly reviewing the list of Designated Persons and maintain a register of Designated Persons, and will notify relevant individuals of their inclusion on or removal from the register.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An executive outside section 4.2 today can be brought within it at the Managing Director's discretion, so any structure entered by a non-Designated employee should be documented to survive, or be unwound on, later designation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If it becomes apparent that a Director has breached this policy, APA Group will give careful consideration to whether it ought to make an announcement to the market explaining the circumstances of the breach and what, if any, remedial and/or disciplinary action it has taken.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach by a Director carries express reputational exposure through a possible market announcement, raising the stakes on any structure that sits close to the 4.2.5 line.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for a Director or Designated Person under this policy. Section 4.2.5 prohibits them at any time, expressly including outside Closed Periods, from entering any hedging instrument or arrangement regarding, or any derivative financial product issued over, any APA Securities they hold, so both the purchased put and the written call are banned outright, whatever the vesting state of the shares and with no clearance route; the section 4.2.7 exceptional circumstances power relieves only against dealing during a Closed Period and does not touch section 4.2.5. The financing leg fails independently: APA Securities may be charged only as part of a diversified portfolio under a margin loan or secured financing arrangement whose terms do not permit title to the securities to be transferred, which excludes a loan secured solely on the collared parcel and any title-transfer or rehypothecation collateral, and unvested or holding-locked securities can never be charged at all. Charged securities remain subject to the policy, so a margin call or lender enforcement sale during a Closed Period needs exceptional circumstances permission from the Chairman rather than being an excluded dealing. These restrictions extend to Related Parties, and the Managing Director can add executives to the Designated Persons register at any time; only employees and contractors outside section 4.2 are unconstrained, and they are the wrong client for this product.
